The 2024 PBM reform law (Act 77) was supposed to fix this, but pharmacists are still drowning in predatory reimbursement rates that don’t cover drug costs. Rite Aid’s bankruptcy proves even big chains can’t survive Washington’s rigged payment schemes.

PBMs like CVS Caremark and OptumRx aren’t lowering prices—they’re bleeding pharmacies dry while bureaucrats pocket profits. Until D.C. breaks Big Pharma’s grip and forces pricing transparency, taxpayers will keep funding this corruption while main street pharmacies vanish.

The Veterans' ACCESS Act (H.R. 5108) proves privatization isn't about improving care—it's about redirecting $27B annually from VA hospitals to corporate middlemen. Rural veterans face 63% longer travel times under this scheme, per Congressional Budget Office analysis.

But let's cut through the noise: The real issue is VA's bloated bureaucracy. Section 4(c) of the ACCESS Act allows private contractors to charge 22% more per patient than VA facilities while delivering worse outcomes. That's not efficiency—it's theft.

The FARM Act (S. 1202) shows how to actually support rural communities—by investing in local infrastructure, not outsourcing care to profit-driven corporations. Veterans deserve medical sovereignty, not another layer of corporate billing departments. Accountability matters. Exposing waste ≠ attacking care. Real reform starts with auditing the 83,000 administrative bloat positions added since 2021, not stripping frontline workers' collective bargaining rights to report mismanagement.

Congressional oversight and public scrutiny are overdue—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/LUzo5SITRY
